messages:
Ana: Quick follow-up on the continuous-batching migration proposal. TL;DR: prefer soft per-tenant queues + small shared emergency pool to avoid worst-case headroom waste. Posting steps and checklist.
Ben: can you summarize the main tradeoffs again? especially around KV cache pressure and p99 spikes.
Ana: sure — high level: per-tenant soft queues = better fairness & tail isolation, but costs extra enqueue bookkeeping and can increase KV cache churn due to more frequent microbatches. shared pool = absorbs bursts from noisy tenants but can starve small tenants if not sized correctly.
Li: how small is "small" for the shared pool? any heuristic?
Ana: thinking 10-15% of total slots initially. heuristic: set to max(quantile(tenant_burst_bytes, 95), 0.12 * total_slots) and revisit after 2 weeks.
Sam: what about admission credits and headroom signaling? we currently use global headroom + tenant reservations. mixing per-tenant will need a fast credit-exchange path.
Zara: +1 on that. we should avoid synchronous cross-node coordination on every enqueue. propose token-bucket locally and async reconciliation.
Mike: does anyone have a microbenchmark plan? i can run canaries.
Ana: yup. plan: 1) unit tests for enqueue/dequeue invariants, 2) single-node perf runs to measure per-tenant overhead, 3) cluster canary with 50 tenants (range small->huge), 4) 1% prod canary with forced noisy tenant.
Ben: suggest adding KV-cache hit tracking per-tenant to the telemetry so we can see churn correlation.
Li: agree. also capture avg batch size and microbatch frequency per tenant.
Sam: realistic load command i used locally: ```./tools/loadtest --tenants 200 --qps 600 --seq 128 --noise 0.1```
Zara: thanks. i ran a quick sim this morning, rough numbers: per-tenant queues add ~6-9% CPU for enqueue bookkeeping, p95 latency improved for small tenants by ~18%, but p99 for large tenants saw a slight increase when shared_pool_size=0.05.
Ana: good to know. that reinforces starting with 0.12-0.15 shared pool.
Ben: rollout/RFC follow-up: we need a migration path for persisted queue state. do we drain and rebuild at restart, or migrate on the fly?
Li: draining is simpler but causes a short window of degraded throughput. on-the-fly requires careful dual-write semantics.
Zara: we could do dual-mode: start with a "compat" mode where new enqueues go to per-tenant queues while old queues are drained naturally; after N hours, flip the default.
Mike: what about canary fallback? feature-flag that flips routing per shard. if p99 regresses above threshold, auto-flip back.
Ana: exactly — implement hitch detection: if p99_increase > 10% && error_rate > 0.5% for 5m then revert. put guardrails in control-plane so we can rollback quickly.
deploy-bot: scheduler-ci report: canary-run-1766667800: baseline p99=182ms -> per-tenant migration candidate p99=198ms (+8.8%), p95=44ms -> 36ms (-18%). errors: 0.12% -> 0.14%. full logs: https://ci.redwood/scheduler/canary/1766667800
Ben: that looks within acceptable limits for initial canary but need to watch long-tail steady state.
Li: for config, propose default snippet: ```
queue_mode: soft-per-tenant
shared_pool_size: 0.15
local_token_bucket_rate: 1200
reconciliation_interval_sec: 10
hitch_detection: {p99_threshold_pct: 10, error_rate_pct: 0.5, window_sec: 300}
```
Sam: we should also document the API changes for the batching operator: new hooks for pre-enqueue hint (priority_hint, kv_affinity) so we can keep cache-friendly placements.
Zara: agree. adding a small opt-in header now avoids breaking current fastpath.
Mike: i'll run the 50-tenant cluster canary tomorrow morning and forward metrics. can someone own rolling rollback playbook?
Ana: Ben, can you own rollback runbook + dashboards? Ben: yup.
Ben: i will add dashboards for per-tenant avg batch size, kv-cache-hit-rate, p95/p99, enqueue CPU, and shared_pool_utilization.
Li: one more thought — quantization/packing might interact badly with microbatching. add a test that mixes long-short sequences to measure interference.
Ana: noted. action items: 1) Mike: run cluster canary + perf dump (due 24h). 2) Ben: rollback runbook + dashboards (48h). 3) Li & Zara: telemetry hooks and API hint header (48h). 4) Sam: add test matrix for sequence-length interference (72h).
Zara: i'll draft the RFC follow-up doc with migration steps and metrics required for GA.
Ana: thanks. if anyone sees anything obviously missing call it out now. otherwise we'll iterate in the RFC doc tomorrow. :thumbsup:
Mike: noted. starting cluster canary at 0600 UTC.
deploy-bot: scheduled deploy: canary/scheduler/1766670000 -> started at 1766670000
Ana: great — keep updates in this thread and drop the canary link when done.
Ben: will do.
